observations: Files I actually read: the request JSON (page 03 script, requiredTransitions and the recorded first reading), source/original.txt and source/REVISION-2026-11-11.md (Requests 1 and 2 and the r13 caption change). I opened these images with Read and looked at them: workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-03.png, workflow/storyboards/page-03.png and workflow/review/page-03.png. I grepped the text and label rect of storyboards-unnumbered/page-03.svg and the beat text of storyboards/page-03.svg. No file was unreadable.

The PNGs match the SVGs. The SVG captions are 'A later morning: / patients can always check / in at the front desk.', 'Some check in ahead / on the Welbuk Health app.', 'Ravi scans the QR / code at the door.', 'A short form on / his own phone, / shared with consent.' and 'Every check-in gets / a slot on the screen.'. The label 'A-10 · A-11 · A-12' is in a rect at (664,1012,305x74), as drawn. The numbered PNG adds only the five beat footers.

The script matches the source, page 3 panels 1-5. All five captions and the TV label are verbatim. The page has no speech, so no question-and-answer pairs exist. The three check-in routes (front desk, app, QR) follow the user's Request 2. The revision note confirms that Ravi is the QR patient, so his own sequence continues on page 4.

Raman and Priya are not named anywhere on the page. That is acceptable because their roles are carried by the captions ('patients can always check in at the front desk', 'Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app') and by the art: an elderly man at the counter with Meera typing, and a young woman tapping a phone check-in card outside the clinic awning.

Unnumbered scan: a Z-pattern of five top-left captions in a 2-2-1 grid, then the teal slot label on the right of the bottom tier. Each panel has one caption at its top left, so the order cannot be ambiguous.

First-reader concern: the link between Ravi and A-12 is only implied. The preview supports it in three ways that agree. (a) The check-in order on the page is Raman in 03-1, Priya in 03-2 and Ravi in 03-3/03-4. (b) In 03-5 they sit left to right in that order under the TV, where 'A-10 · A-11 · A-12' runs in the same direction. (c) Page 4 then confirms it explicitly: in 04-1 'Soon, his slot comes up.' appears with 'NOW · A-12' and Ravi standing alone while the two chairs beside him are empty. The mapping is implied on page 3 and confirmed on the next page, which is sufficient. No change is needed.

In 03-4 the placeholder for ravi is a tall box. The preview shows an over-the-shoulder close-up: Ravi's bearded profile at the right, his phone held in both hands, and a thumb on the consent tick-box with the wristwatch visible. The tall face region is a close-up and does not imply a full figure.

In the preview the 03-1 caption covers part of a wall TV behind the desk. It is clear of the faces of Raman and Meera and of Raman's hand and stick. The 03-5 label sits inside the drawn TV screen, so it reads as on-screen text.

transitions.observation: The evening onboarding two-shot is followed by 'A later morning:' over the bright, tidy reception with the QR stand and a TV visible. The caption and the daylight mark the time jump, which answers the page 2 expectation 'What changes for patients once the clinic is set up?'.

From the front desk to the street outside the teal awning: Priya walks in while tapping her phone. The caption 'Some check in ahead...' contrasts with 'can always... front desk', and the clinic doorway in the background ties her to the same clinic.

The scene moves inside the glass entrance. Ravi is named in the caption as he scans the QR stand, and the reception and waiting patients are visible behind him, so it is the same place and the same morning.
The scan in 03-3 is followed by a close-up of the form on the same phone, with the same green shirt, beard and wristwatch. The caption 'his own phone' refers back to Ravi in 03-3.

The consent tap is followed by the wide waiting area, where all three patients from 03-1 to 03-4 sit under the TV slot list. Ravi has the phone in his hand and the bag on his lap (script props), and the caption ties together every route shown on the page.

The same waiting area. 'Soon, his slot comes up.' appears with 'NOW · A-12', Ravi stands with the bag back on his shoulder, and the chairs of Raman and Priya are now empty, so a short wait is implied (04-1 transition: time-change).

readingReview.comparison: My comparison agrees with the recorded first reading: a clear Z-pattern of captions in the intended order [1],[1],[1],[1],[1,2], with no speech and no skipped replies. The first reader's concern is that the connection between Ravi and A-12 is only implied. I judge it acceptable: the order of check-ins, the seating order and the order of the label all agree left to right, and 04-1 states it explicitly with 'his slot' and 'NOW · A-12' while the other two chairs are empty. The tall ravi placeholder in 03-4 is a close-up in the art, not a full figure. The first reader's note that Raman and Priya are never named is acceptable because the captions and art carry their roles. Nothing is left unresolved.
